title: What is Code-Switching?: A Guide for English Learners
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: able to use two languages fluently.
the level of formality used in speech (formal/informal).
a particular way of pronouncing a language.
a regional or social form of a language with unique words and pronunciation.
the ability to speak smoothly and naturally.
when one language affects another, causing mistakes.
happening without thinking or conscious control.

sentences.en: Today we’re going to explore a topic that I notice again and again whenever I work with bilingual people, speak with people who are studying a second language, and actually notice inside my own family: code switching.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨一个我在与双语人士合作、和学习第二语言的人交谈时，甚至在自己的家庭内部一再注意到的主题：语码转换。

sentences.en: You’ve probably done it yourself. You start a sentence in English, suddenly use a word from your native language, then switch back again.
sentences.zh: 你可能自己也做过。你用英语开始一句话，突然用母语说了一个词，然后又切回英语。

sentences.en: This is a form of code switching and is extremely common.
sentences.zh: 这是语码转换的一种形式，而且非常普遍。

sentences.en: Code switching happens all around the world, in every culture, anywhere multilingual people communicate.
sentences.zh: 语码转换在世界各地、各种文化中、任何多元语言人群交流的地方都会发生。

sentences.en: So, what exactly is code switching? Why do bilingual and multilingual speakers mix languages like this?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底什么是语码转换？为什么双语和多语说话者会这样混用语言？

sentences.en: Is it a sign that your English is improving?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是你英语在进步的信号吗？

sentences.en: Or could it be something that slows down your progress?
sentences.zh: 还是说，这可能会放慢你的进步速度？

sentences.en: In this episode, we’re going to break it down clearly and practically.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将进行清晰而实用的剖析。

sentences.en: We’ll look at what code switching is, why people do it, and most importantly how to manage code switching as a language learner!
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨什么是语码转换、人们为什么这样做，最重要的是，作为语言学习者如何应对语码转换！

sentences.en: So what exactly is code switching? Code switching is when a speaker alternates between two or more languages or even different varieties of the same language within a single conversation, sentence or interaction.
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟什么是语码转换？语码转换是指说话者在同一段对话、一句话或互动中，在两种或多种语言、甚至同一种语言的不同变体之间进行交替使用。

sentences.en: It can be a full sentence, a quick phrase, or just a word.
sentences.zh: 它可以是一个完整的句子、一个简短的短语，或者仅仅是一个词。

sentences.en: For example, you might be speaking English, but suddenly switch into Spanish to express an emotion or use a phrase that feels easier or more natural in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可能在讲英语，但突然切换到西班牙语来表达一种情绪，或者使用一个在西班牙语中感觉更轻松、更自然的短语。

sentences.en: Then without thinking, you switch right back to English.
sentences.zh: 然后不假思索地，你马上切换回英语。

sentences.en: This isn’t unusual. It’s a product, or a part, of being multilingual.
sentences.zh: 这并不罕见。这是精通多语言的产物，或者说是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Code switching happens naturally in conversations where people share more than one language, and your brain is simply using all of the tools, all of the knowledge, it has available.
sentences.zh: 语码转换在人们使用一种以上语言的对话中自然发生，你的大脑只是在调用它所拥有的所有工具和所有知识。

sentences.en: It’s not necessarily a mistake or a sign of poor ability.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是个错误，也不是能力差的信号。

sentences.en: In fact, some linguists argue that it shows advanced communication skills because your brain is selecting vocabulary and grammar from multiple different language systems at the same time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些语言学家认为，这显示了高级的沟通技巧，因为你的大脑在同时从多个不同的语言系统中选择词汇和语法。

sentences.en: Code switching doesn’t only mean changing from one language to another.
sentences.zh: 语码转换不仅指从一种语言变成另一种语言。

sentences.en: It can also involve switching accents. For example, speaking differently with family than with your workmates.
sentences.zh: 它还可能涉及口音的切换。例如，和家人说话时与和同事说话时语气不同。

sentences.en: It could involve switching dialects. For example, using regional vocabulary or pronunciation depending on who you’re talking to.
sentences.zh: 它可能涉及方言的切换。例如，根据你正在交谈的对象使用区域词汇或发音。

sentences.en: Or it could be switching levels of formality.
sentences.zh: 或者它可能是正式程度的切换。

sentences.en: Being more professional at work, and then casual or slangy with your friends.
sentences.zh: 在工作时更专业，然后和朋友在一起时更随性或满口俚语。

sentences.en: Every time you adjust how you speak depending on where you are, who you’re talking to or what you want to express, you are switching between different codes.
sentences.zh: 每次你根据自己所在的地方、交谈的对象或想要表达的内容来调整说话方式时，你就是在不同的语码之间进行切换。

sentences.en: Code switching comes in quite a few different forms.
sentences.zh: 语码转换有相当多的不同形式。

sentences.en: I think that understanding these forms will help you notice your own habits and use them more intentionally as a language learner.
sentences.zh: 我认为理解这些形式将帮助你注意到自己的习惯，并作为语言学习者更有意识地使用它们。

sentences.en: I will also demonstrate these types of code switching with Japanese and English.
sentences.zh: 我还会用日语和英语来演示这些类型的语码转换。

sentences.en: This is because I actually do code switch every day between Japanese and English, as I communicate with my wife in a mix of Japanese and English.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我每天确实会在日语和英语之间进行语码转换，因为我和妻子交流时使用的是日语和英语的混合体。

sentences.en: The first type of code switching is inter-sentential switching.
sentences.zh: 第一种语码转换是句间转换。

sentences.en: This is a type of switching that happens between sentences.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在句子之间发生的转换。

sentences.en: You finish one sentence in one language and the next sentence comes out in a different language.
sentences.zh: 你用一种语言说完一句话，下一句话就用另一种语言说出来了。

sentences.en: In my case, I often finish one sentence in Japanese and the next sentence comes out in English.
sentences.zh: 对我的情况来说，我经常用日语说完一句话，然后下一句话就用英语说出来了。

sentences.en: For example, “Kyō wa metcha isogashikatta.
sentences.zh: 例如，“Kyō wa metcha isogashikatta.

sentences.en: Anyway, I’m glad I’m home.” This means, “I was so busy today.
sentences.zh: Anyway, I’m glad I’m home.” 这意思是，“我今天太忙了。

sentences.en: Anyway, I’m glad I’m home now.” Because the switch happens at a sentence boundary, this type of code switching is often more deliberate.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我很高兴我到家了。”因为转换发生在句子边界，这种类型的语码转换通常更有意图。

sentences.en: It commonly occurs when the speaker changes the topic or the tone or maybe responds to a new person.
sentences.zh: 它通常发生在说话者改变话题、语气或可能在回应一个新人的时候。

sentences.en: The next type of code switching is intra-sentential switching.
sentences.zh: 下一类型的语码转换是句内转换。

sentences.en: This is when you mix languages inside the same sentence.
sentences.zh: 这是指你在同一句话内部混用语言。

sentences.en: It’s extremely common among bilingual speakers because the brain can move smoothly between languages in real time.
sentences.zh: 这在双语说话者中极其普遍，因为大脑可以在实时中在语言之间流畅地移动。

sentences.en: For example, “The weather today is ‘metcha’ cold.”
sentences.zh: 例如，“The weather today is ‘metcha’ cold.”

sentences.en: I used a Japanese adverb meaning “very” in the middle of the sentence.
sentences.zh: 我在句子的中间使用了一个意思是“非常”的日语副词。

sentences.en: These switches can be single words, short phrases, sometimes longer chunks of language, but often short words.
sentences.zh: 这些转换可以是单个词、短短语，有时是更长的语言块，但通常是简短的词。

sentences.en: And most bilingual speakers don’t even realize they’re doing it.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数双语说话者甚至没有意识到他们在这样做。

sentences.en: It’s usually fast and expressive and very efficient.
sentences.zh: 它通常很快、很有表现力且非常高效。

sentences.en: Another form of code switching is tag switching.
sentences.zh: 另一种形式的语码转换是标签转换。

sentences.en: Tag switching involves adding small expressions from another language at the end of your sentence to add emotion or emphasis.
sentences.zh: 标签转换包括在句子末尾添加来自另一种语言的小表达，以增加情感或强调。

sentences.en: It would be like saying a sentence in your native language, but ending with an English word like, “right?” Or “you know.” Or in my case.
sentences.zh: 这就像用你的母语说一句话，但以一个英语词结尾，比如，“对吧？”或者“你知道的。”或者以我为例。

sentences.en: “It’s really difficult, ‘ne.'” ‘ Ne ‘ is a very common sentence tag in Japanese that kind of has the meaning of, “isn’t it” in English.
sentences.zh: “It’s really difficult, ‘ne.’” ‘Ne’ 是日语中非常常见的句尾标签，在英语里有点像是“对吧”的意思。

sentences.en: These short tags help express humor or identity, and they usually slip into speech naturally and rarely disrupt the grammar of the main sentence.
sentences.zh: 这些简短的标签有助于表达幽默或身份认同，它们通常自然地滑入言语中，极少破坏主句的语法。

sentences.en: Finally, not all code switching requires two languages.
sentences.zh: 最后，并非所有的语码转换都需要两种语言。

sentences.en: Sometimes we switch between different styles of the same language.
sentences.zh: 有时我们在同一种语言的不同风格之间切换。

sentences.en: Depending on where we are, who we’re speaking to, or how we want to sound, we can switch our register.
sentences.zh: 根据我们所在的地方、我们正在和谁说话、或者我们想要听起来怎么样，我们可以切换语域。

sentences.en: This is why it’s often called register switching or style switching.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它通常被称为语域转换或风格转换。

sentences.en: For example, when you’re at work: “Good afternoon everyone.”
sentences.zh: 例如，当你在工作时：“下午好，各位。”

sentences.en: W hen you’re with your friends: “Hey, what’s up?”
sentences.zh: 当你在和朋友在一起时：“嘿，最近怎么样？”

sentences.en: Even though you are still speaking English, you’ve switched between formal and informal styles.
sentences.zh: 尽管你仍然在说英语，但你已经在正式和非正式风格之间进行了切换。

sentences.en: You are adjusting your “code” to match the situation.
sentences.zh: 你正在调整你的“语码”来匹配当前的状况。

sentences.en: So why do bilingual and multilingual speakers switch languages so naturally?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么双语和多语说话者会如此自然地切换语言呢？

sentences.en: In most cases, it’s not a conscious decision.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，这不是一个有意识的决定。

sentences.en: There are several reasons behind it, and many of them happen automatically.
sentences.zh: 这背后有几个原因，其中许多都是自动发生的。

sentences.en: We don’t think about it. Language isn’t just a tool for communication.
sentences.zh: 我们不会去思考它。语言不仅仅是沟通的工具。

sentences.en: It’s also connected to the community we belong to or the relationships we have.
sentences.zh: 它还与我们所属的社群或我们拥有的人际关系息息相关。

sentences.en: Code switching can strengthen your sense of belonging.
sentences.zh: 语码转换可以增强你的归属感。

sentences.en: In many cases, certain emotions feel more authentic or real in a specific language.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，某些情感在特定的语言中会感觉更真实或更真切。

sentences.en: You might communicate day to day in English, but argue or express love in your native language.
sentences.zh: 你可能日常生活中用英语交流，但吵架或表达爱意时会用你的母语。

sentences.en: This is because your native language is more powerful or emotional for you.
sentences.zh: 这是因为你的母语对你来说更有力量或更有情感色彩。

sentences.en: Switching languages allows people to communicate feelings more accurately and naturally.
sentences.zh: 切换语言使人们能够更准确、更自然地传达情感。

sentences.en: Code switching can also be purely efficient.
sentences.zh: 语码转换也可以纯粹是为了效率。

sentences.en: Instead of searching for the correct word in one language, many bilinguals just pick the quickest or clearest option from whichever language fits their idea.
sentences.zh: 许多双语者不会费力去寻找某种语言中的正确词汇，而是直接从最符合他们想法的语言中挑选最快或最清晰的选项。

sentences.en: There’s also the influence of topic shifts.
sentences.zh: 还有话题转变的影响。

sentences.en: Different aspects of life often feel tied to specific languages.
sentences.zh: 生活的不同方面通常感觉与特定的语言紧密相连。

sentences.en: Many English learners, you guys listening, use English for work, maybe study, but you switch to your native language when you’re discussing personal things.
sentences.zh: 许多英语学习者，也就是正在听节目的你们，用英语工作、也许还有学习，但当你们讨论私事时，会切换回母语。

sentences.en: One language might dominate your professional life while another belongs to your home life.
sentences.zh: 一种语言可能支配你的职业生活，而另一种语言则属于你的家庭生活。

sentences.en: Another reason for code switching is who we’re talking to.
sentences.zh: 语码转换的另一个原因是我们的交谈对象。

sentences.en: We change how we speak based on who we’re talking to.
sentences.zh: 我们根据交谈的对象来改变说话方式。

sentences.en: I talk in English with my wife most of the time, but as soon as a member of her family enters the room, we switch to Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都和妻子用英语交谈，但只要她家里的某个人走进房间，我们就切换成日语。

sentences.en: Then there’s the simplest explanation… habit and convenience.
sentences.zh: 接下来是最简单的解释……习惯和便利。

sentences.en: When you live between two languages, both systems are active in your mind.
sentences.zh: 当你生活在两种语言之间时，两个系统在你的大脑中都是活跃的。

sentences.en: Words pop up from whichever language comes fastest, and switching happens automatically.
sentences.zh: 词汇会从最快浮现的语言中蹦出来，而转换则是自动发生的。

sentences.en: It’s just how multilingual brains work. So why does code switching matter for people learning English?
sentences.zh: 多语大脑就是这样工作的。那么，为什么语码转换对学习英语的人很重要呢？

sentences.en: I think understanding this can help you use your native language as a tool to learn more effectively without letting it slow you down.
sentences.zh: 我认为理解这一点可以帮助你把母语当作一种工具，更有效地学习，同时不让它拖慢你的进度。

sentences.en: Learning to manage code switching consciously is a part of becoming a better English speaker.
sentences.zh: 学会清醒地管理语码转换，是成为一名更出色的英语演讲者的一个部分。

sentences.en: In some cases, your first language can help you think through what you say.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，你的第一语言可以帮你理清你想说的话。

sentences.en: It can help you maybe plan ideas before speaking, translate difficult grammar, and check the meaning of a new word.
sentences.zh: 它或许能在你说话前帮你构思想法、翻译困难的语法，并检查新单词的意思。

sentences.en: It’s kind of like having a dictionary in your head if you are bilingual.
sentences.zh: 如果你是双语者，这有点像在脑子里装了一本字典。

sentences.en: But it can become a problem. It becomes a problem when code switching turns into an unconscious habit.
sentences.zh: 但它可能会变成一个问题。当语码转换变成一种无意识的习惯时，它就成了问题。

sentences.en: When you switch languages every time something feels difficult.
sentences.zh: 每当遇到困难的事情时你就切换语言。

sentences.en: If your brain constantly returns to your native language for comfort, you will lose valuable practice time in English.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑为了寻求舒适而不断退回到母语中，你就会失去宝贵的英语练习时间。

sentences.en: I see this at my conversation clubs occasionally.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔在我的英语角俱乐部里看到这种情况。

sentences.en: For example, if I make a conversation room with multiple speakers of the same language, maybe multiple Spanish speakers, when these people don’t know an English word, maybe they switch to Spanish without thinking.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我建了一个有多个相同母语发言者的聊天室，比如好几个西班牙语使用者，当这些人不知道一个英语单词时，他们可能会不假思索地切换到西班牙语。

sentences.en: This is one of the reasons I try my best to mix languages at the conversation clubs.
sentences.zh: 这也是我尽最大努力在英语角俱乐部里混用语言的原因之一。

sentences.en: The habit of code switching when things get difficult slows down the development of your automatic fluency.
sentences.zh: 当事情变难时就进行语码转换的习惯会减慢你自动流利度的发展。

sentences.en: It slows down your ability to think and speak quickly without translating.
sentences.zh: 它会减慢你无需翻译就能快速思考和说话的能力。

sentences.en: It can also hide gaps in your vocabulary or your grammar.
sentences.zh: 它还会掩盖你词汇或语法上的漏洞。

sentences.en: It can hide your weaknesses, because switching helps you avoid challenging areas instead of learning them.
sentences.zh: 它能掩盖你的弱点，因为切换能帮你避开具有挑战性的领域，而不是去攻克它们。

sentences.en: There are also always communication issues to consider.
sentences.zh: 还有一些沟通问题总是需要考虑的。

sentences.en: In mixed language groups, code switching into a language that not everyone understands can leave people out even if you don’t mean to be rude.
sentences.zh: 在混合语言的群体中，切换到并非所有人都懂的语言可能会把人冷落，即使你并非故意无礼。

sentences.en: In professional or international contexts, code switching languages in the middle of a sentence or a discussion can seem unprofessional or secretive, especially if people don’t know what you’re saying.
sentences.zh: 在职场或国际环境中，在句子或讨论的中途切换语言可能会显得不够专业或神神秘秘，尤其是当别人听不懂你在说什么的时候。

sentences.en: Beyond communication, code switching can lead to interference between languages.
sentences.zh: 除了沟通，语码转换还会导致语言之间的干扰。

sentences.en: When your brain jumps quickly between language systems, things like grammar and word order can accidentally carry over incorrectly from one language to another.
sentences.zh: 当你的大脑在语言系统之间快速跳跃时，语法和语序之类的事情可能会无意中从一种语言错误地带入另一种语言。

sentences.en: And of course, this can result in mistakes.
sentences.zh: 当然，这会导致错误。

sentences.en: As English learners, you also need to understand that code switching doesn’t only happen between languages.
sentences.zh: 作为英语学习者，你们还需要明白，语码转换不仅发生在不同语言之间。

sentences.en: It also occurs inside English when switching between formal and informal styles.
sentences.zh: 它也发生在英语内部正式风格和非正式风格的切换中。

sentences.en: Speaking too casually in a professional situation or using too formal language with friends can give the wrong impression.
sentences.zh: 在职场环境中说话过于随意，或者在朋友面前使用过于正式的语言，都会给人留下错误的印象。

sentences.en: So knowing when to switch your register is just as important as knowing when to switch languages.
sentences.zh: 所以，知道何时切换语域与知道何时切换语言同样重要。

sentences.en: Let’s end this episode with some advice on how to manage code switching effectively.
sentences.zh: 让我们以一些关于如何有效管理语码转换的建议来结束本期节目。

sentences.en: Before switching languages, you should try and ask yourself, Are you switching because it really helps you?
sentences.zh: 在切换语言之前，你应该试着问问自己，你切换是因为它真的对你有帮助吗？

sentences.en: Or are you switching just because you are avoiding English?
sentences.zh: 还是说你切换仅仅是因为你在逃避英语？

sentences.en: Conscious switching, thinking about it, can be useful, but automatic switching can stop you from practicing your English properly.
sentences.zh: 有意识地切换，即对此进行思考，可能会很有用，但自动切换会阻止你正确地练习英语。

sentences.en: Force yourself to just use English. Maybe incorporate English only sessions into your daily life.
sentences.zh: 强迫自己只使用英语。也许可以将纯英语时段融入你的日常生活中。

sentences.en: Set aside five or 10 minutes where you speak or think only in English, and don’t allow yourself to speak any words from your native language.
sentences.zh: 留出五到十分钟的时间，只用英语交谈或思考，不允许自己说出任何母语单词。

sentences.en: It could be talking to yourself or writing a journal or having a conversation.
sentences.zh: 这可以是自言自语、写日记或进行对话。

sentences.en: Maybe join one of my conversation clubs.
sentences.zh: 也许可以加入我的英语角俱乐部之一。

sentences.en: Many code switches happen because you simply just don’t know the right word in that situation.
sentences.zh: 许多语码转换的发生，纯粹是因为你在那种情况下不知道正确的单词。

sentences.en: So if possible, and this won’t always be possible, but if possible, before you have a meeting or a class or a conversation, prepare a list of vocabulary that are specific to that topic.
sentences.zh: 所以如果可能的话——虽然这并不总是可能——但如果可能的话，在开会、上课或交谈之前，准备一份特定于该主题的词汇表。

sentences.en: Having the words ready will reduce your temptation to switch to your first language.
sentences.zh: 把单词准备好会减少你切换到第一语言的冲动。

sentences.en: So if you know you have a meeting coming up about the sales for a product, make a list of sales vocabulary specific to that product so that you don’t have to worry about getting it wrong.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你知道接下来有一场关于某产品销售的会议，请列出一份针对该产品的销售专属词汇表，这样你就不用担心弄错了。

sentences.en: You could also try to speak English for longer stretches.
sentences.zh: 你也可以尝试连续更长时间地讲英语。

sentences.en: For example, listen to something like a podcast or a short dialogue in English, and then repeat it out loud without switching.
sentences.zh: 例如，听一听播客或英语短对话之类的东西，然后大声复述而不进行切换。

sentences.en: This kind of helps to train your brain maintain English even when the conversation is challenging.
sentences.zh: 这有助于训练你的大脑在对话充满挑战时依然保持英语输出。

sentences.en: If you are speaking in a group where not everyone understands your native language, be very careful about code switching.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个并非所有人都懂你母语的群体中说话，请务必小心语码转换。

sentences.en: If you do, make sure everyone understands what you said, so no one feels excluded.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做了，请确保每个人都听懂了你所说的话，这样就不会有人感到被排挤了。

sentences.en: And finally, remember that code switching doesn’t only happen between languages, it also happens between formal and informal English, and regional and standard English.
sentences.zh: 最后，请记住，语码转换不仅发生在不同的语言之间，它也发生在正式与非正式英语之间，以及地方英语与标准英语之间。

sentences.en: Practice different registers consciously.
sentences.zh: 有意识地练习不同的语域。

sentences.en: For example, understand the difference in your language at a professional meeting versus chatting with friends.
sentences.zh: 例如，理解你在职业会议上的语言与和朋友闲聊时的语言之间的差异。

sentences.en: This can help reduce any accidental mistakes and improve your confidence in any setting.
sentences.zh: 这可以帮助减少任何意外的错误，并提高你在任何环境下的自信心。

sentences.en: By managing code switching intentionally, I think you can use it as a tool instead of letting it become a barrier to your learning.​
sentences.zh: 通过有意识地管理语码转换，我认为你可以把它当作一个工具，而不是让它成为你学习的障碍。

sentences.en: Code switching is a natural part of living with more than one language.
sentences.zh: 语码转换是使用一种以上语言生活时的自然组成部分。

sentences.en: It’s not something to be ashamed of, and it’s not automatically a sign of weak English skills.
sentences.zh: 这没什么好羞耻的，它也不是英语能力薄弱的自动信号。

sentences.en: It shows that you have more than one way to think, feel, and communicate.
sentences.zh: 它表明你有不止一种思考、感受和交流的方式。

sentences.en: Becoming fluent in English does not mean eliminating your native language.
sentences.zh: 英语说得流利并不意味着要消灭你的母语。

sentences.en: It means choosing when and how to use it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要选择何时以及如何使用它。

sentences.en: When you stay in English long enough to struggle, your brain will grow stronger.
sentences.zh: 当你留在英语环境中足够久去面对挣扎时，你的大脑就会变得更强大。

sentences.en: When you switch to your native language to avoid challenges, you will delay that growth.
sentences.zh: 当你为了逃避挑战而切换到母语时，你就会延迟这种成长。

sentences.en: Don’t try to stop code switching. Instead, learn to control it.
sentences.zh: 不要试图阻止语码转换。相反，要学会控制它。

sentences.en: Let your first language support your English, but don’t let it protect you from the hard work that leads to fluency.
sentences.zh: 让你的母语来支持你的英语，但不要让它保护你免受通往流利所需的艰苦工作的冲击。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Let me know your opinion about code switching.
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看呢？让我知道你对语码转换的看法。

sentences.en: Do you notice yourself code switching while speaking English or speaking to your friends or in different situations?
sentences.zh: 你在说英语、和朋友交谈或在不同情况下说话时，有没有注意到自己在进行语码转换？
